study_identification_part.si_4_title: Fractionating autism based on neuroanatomical normative modeling

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Gaussian process regression (GPR) was used to estimate normative models of cortical thickness across the cortical surface. The model was trained on 206 neurotypical participants to predict vertex-wise cortical thickness. The study used 10-fold cross-validation during training.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: Gaussian process regression (GPR) was used to estimate a normative model of CT across the cortical surface. GPR was trained on the NT cohort (N=206) using the following covariates

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Vertex-wise cortical thickness (CT) was the response variable, estimated from T1-weighted MRI using FreeSurfer version 5.3. Cortical thickness maps were smoothed with a 10-mm surface-based Gaussian kernel.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: Cortical thickness was estimated from the high-resolution T1-weighted image for each subject using FreeSurfer version 5.3...These covariates were used to predict CT as a response (dependent) variable
nm2_2_response_variable.location: 41398_2020_1057_MOESM1_ESM.docx.md: Supplementary Methods / Magnetic Resonance Imaging; Normative modelling

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: The normative model included age and sex as primary covariates, full-scale IQ (FIQ) as a covariate, the FreeSurfer Euler number as a proxy for image/scan quality, and dummy-coded site variables to account for multi-site acquisition (6 sites).
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: GPR was trained on the NT cohort (N=206) using the following covariates (i.e. independent variables): age, sex, full-scale IQ (FIQ), the Freesurfer Euler number indicating the topological complexity of the reconstructed cortical surface and which has been validated as a surrogate marker for image quality, plus dummy coded variables representing data acquisition sites.
